entry.subject: Dual-battery alternating support / regeneration buffer
entry.trigger: Proposal to use two batteries alternately, with one acting mainly as a support mechanism for Axle rotation rather than as the sole source of shaft power.
result: Two batteries do not change the conservation-of-energy boundary, but they can materially improve startup reserve, transient support, regenerative headroom, redundancy and measurement clarity.
A support pack can supply only the instantaneous torque/power deficit required to hold target RPM while hydraulic/process torque carries the rest.
A separate recovery pack can remain intentionally below full SOC so AFPM regeneration and verified process surplus are not clipped by a full support battery.
Battery roles may alternate under BMS/DC-bus supervision to balance cycle wear and preserve restart capability.
The authoritative energy proof uses E_A + E_B, not either battery separately; swapping roles cannot turn internal energy transfer into generation.
entry.next_measurement: Compare single-pack versus dual-pack startup/support Wh, converter losses, regenerative capture and total E_A+E_B over the same hydraulic/load cycle.
